title: Salman Khan Is About to Play a Warrior King — and Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra Will Direct Him
excerpt: The Rang De Basanti filmmaker is directing Salman in a two-part period epic for Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment. It's their first collaboration, and it sounds enormous.
body:
Here's a sentence Bollywood has never produced before: **Salman Khan**, **Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra**, and **Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment** are coming together for a two-part historical action drama. If that lineup doesn't make you sit up, check your pulse.

According to a Bollywood Hungama exclusive, Salman is in advanced talks with Excel Entertainment for a grand period saga helmed by the National Award-winning director behind *Rang De Basanti* and *Bhaag Milkha Bhaag*. The film will reportedly tell the story of one of India's most iconic warrior figures, split across two cinematic chapters — the kind of canvas that Mehra has spent his career earning the right to paint on.

> "Salman Khan is looking to sign on for big projects and believes that the Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra film will do justice to his larger-than-life aura. He has heard the script and was bowled over by the characteristics of his part." — Source, Bollywood Hungama

The kicker? Salman will reportedly undergo a **complete physical transformation** for the role. This isn't another *Dabangg*-style swagger project — this is a period warrior who demands a different body, a different bearing, a different kind of Salman entirely. Think less Chulbul Pandey, more Maharana.

## The Slate That Made History Jealous

What makes this even more extraordinary is the context. Salman Khan hasn't had a lineup this ambitious in over a decade. He's currently shooting **Vamshi Paidipally's untitled action drama** with **Nayanthara** (locked for Eid 2027). By October, he pivots to his first-ever superhero film with **Raj and DK**, the masterminds behind *The Family Man*. And once that wraps, he walks straight into Mehra's period universe — likely kicking off shooting by **Summer 2027**.

That's three radically different genres back-to-back: a commercial action entertainer, a superhero comedy, and a two-part historical epic. This is a 60-year-old superstar recalibrating his entire career in one year.

## Why This Pairing Matters

**Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra** is one of Indian cinema's most visually ambitious directors. *Rang De Basanti* rewired how a generation thought about patriotism and rebellion. *Bhaag Milkha Bhaag* turned a sports biopic into a visceral emotional experience. *Delhi-6* had its flaws, but nobody questioned its ambition. When Mehra does period, he brings texture — dust on skin, weight in armor, stillness before violence.

Salman, for all his stardom, has never worked with a filmmaker of this particular sensibility. His closest brush with historical drama was *Veer* in 2010, and the less said about that, the better. But Mehra isn't Anil Sharma. If anyone can extract the actor hiding inside the superstar, it's the man who turned Aamir Khan into Daljeet and Farhan Akhtar into Milkha Singh.

**Farhan Akhtar** producing through Excel adds another layer. Excel has built its reputation on smart, scaled storytelling — *Dil Chahta Hai*, *Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara*, *Mirzapur*, *The Family Man*. A Salman Khan period epic is new territory for the banner, and it suggests this won't be the kind of historical film that confuses volume for grandeur.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRI audiences, this is the kind of announcement that recalibrates expectations. Salman Khan films have always been reliable event cinema in overseas markets — the opening-weekend-and-done variety. But a Mehra-directed, Excel-produced historical drama designed as a two-part theatrical epic? That's playing a different game entirely.

If the subject is who industry whispers suggest — one of the most popular warrior figures from Indian history — the global appeal could be massive. Period epics with mythological or historical roots have been Bollywood's strongest international export since *Baahubali* proved the format works.

## What Needs to Happen

Salman is yet to sign the dotted lines. Discussions are ongoing around shooting schedules and remuneration, and more clarity is expected toward the end of 2026. But the signal is loud: the man who defined commercial Bollywood for three decades is betting his next phase on filmmakers who don't do easy.

The real question isn't whether Salman will do this film. It's whether he'll disappear into the role the way Mehra's best actors have. If he does, this could be the performance that makes everyone forget *Race 3* ever happened.

And honestly? It's about time.
